generatedBy: Drafted by SI from the build brief and the PSI record text. Reviewed by the EMBER team on 15 November 2026 against the PSI records and the published papers named in each source. A combustion researcher should confirm before this is used for design.
reviewNote: Reviewed by the EMBER team on 15 November 2026. A combustion researcher should confirm before this is used for design.

defaults.reason: BASS ran in the Microgravity Science Glovebox at about 1 atm. Most burns used cabin air at about 21 to 22 percent oxygen. A NASA presentation shows some burns at about 17 percent after nitrogen was added, and the table does not say which. A nitrogen jet was also tested as an extinguisher.
defaults.source: Ferkul and co-authors, BASS, ASGSR 2013, NTRS 20140011099: "Ambient oxygen atmospheres 17% to 21.5% (cabin air)." NASA, A Researcher's Guide to Combustion Science, 2015, page 19: tests "as low as 17 percent oxygen".

defaults.reason: SAME overheated spacecraft materials to make smoke for fire detector tests, in the Microgravity Science Glovebox in cabin air at about 1 atm. It is a smoke test, not a fire test. No source states the oxygen or the pressure as a number.
defaults.source: NASA SAME fact sheet: conducted in the Microgravity Science Glovebox on the ISS. Spivey and co-authors, MSG overview, NTRS 20080013594: the work volume is held at least 1.3 mbar below the cabin. Meyer and co-authors, Fire Safety Journal 2018: smoke from oxidative pyrolysis with air flow past the samples.

defaults.reason: SAME-R reused the SAME hardware in the Microgravity Science Glovebox, in cabin air at about 1 atm. Samples were heated below their ignition point, so nothing burned. It is a smoke test for fire detectors.
defaults.source: Urban and co-authors, AIAA 2012-3536, NTRS 20130000422: materials "were heated to temperatures below the ignition point" in the Microgravity Science Glovebox.

defaults.reason: DAFT tested dust counters on a test dust carried in bags filled with nitrogen from the station supply, and on cabin air. Nothing burned. No source gives the oxygen in the bags, so EMBER states no oxygen for these rows and does not plot them.
defaults.source: PSI-47 table, both rows: "Arizona Road Dust (ARD Fine) in combination with ISS GN2". NASA Glenn article, NTRS 20050215648: nitrogen "will be used to fill 15-liter sample bags".

defaults.reason: SPICE burned gas jet flames in a coflow of cabin air in the glovebox.
defaults.source: Dotson and co-authors, Fire Safety Journal 2011: cabin oxygen "within an estimated range of 20–23%". Stocker and co-authors 2014, NTRS 20140009169: "The pressure was consistently ~100 kPa" with "~21% oxygen".

defaults.reason: SLICE used the same flow duct as SPICE, in cabin air.
defaults.source: Stocker and co-authors 2014, NTRS 20140009169: SPICE and SLICE ran in the Microgravity Science Glovebox "using common hardware", at about 100 kPa and 21 percent oxygen.

defaults.reason: Saffire-I ran in the Cygnus cargo vehicle cabin, filled with station air at hatch closing. Olson and co-authors, Table 1, record 102 kPa. Oxygen comes from the table.
defaults.source: Olson and co-authors, Combustion and Flame 2023, doi 10.1016/j.combustflame.2022.112559, Table 1, Flight I: 21.7 percent oxygen at 102 kPa.

defaults.reason: Saffire-II ran in the Cygnus cargo vehicle cabin, filled with station air at hatch closing. Olson and co-authors, Table 1, record 103 kPa, and the Saffire-II PMMA paper gives 100 kPa. Oxygen comes from the table.
defaults.source: Olson and co-authors, Combustion and Flame 2023, doi 10.1016/j.combustflame.2022.112559, Table 1, Flight II samples 5 and 6: 22.1 percent oxygen at 103 kPa.

defaults.reason: Saffire-III ran in the Cygnus cargo vehicle cabin, filled with station air at hatch closing. Olson and co-authors, Table 1, record 21.2 percent oxygen at 99 kPa. The second sample burned after the first, so its oxygen was likely a little lower. The PSI table has no oxygen column.
defaults.source: Olson and co-authors, Combustion and Flame 2023, doi 10.1016/j.combustflame.2022.112559, Table 1, Flight III: 21.2 percent oxygen at 99 kPa.

defaults.reason: BASS-II ran in the Microgravity Science Glovebox at cabin pressure. Oxygen comes from the table.
defaults.source: Zhao and co-authors 2015, NTRS 20150008962: "Ambient pressure was 1 atm."

defaults.reason: The ACME BRE chamber was filled to a chosen pressure for each test, from about 0.56 to 1.07 atm. Tests at 26.5 percent oxygen ran near 0.7 atm and many at 34 percent near 0.56 to 0.6 atm. NASA's table note says: "The chamber pressures were also varied but are not identified in this summary table." So EMBER does not plot these tests.
defaults.source: Dehghani and co-authors, Combustion and Flame 2021, doi 10.1016/j.combustflame.2021.01.035: "pressures of 1 to about 0.56 bar". Dehghani, PhD thesis, University of Maryland 2022, Tables 6.1, E.1 and F.1: 0.565 to 1.08 bar.

defaults.reason: A note in the ACME s-Flame table says the atmosphere is about 1 atm at the start. Pressure rises and oxygen falls during a test day as the sealed chamber fills with products. Oxygen comes from the table. Some days used helium instead of nitrogen.
defaults.source: PSI-23 table note: "Atmosphere is ~1 atm but pressure increases and O2% drops with vitiation."
